transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2028-12-14 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 49 minutes
- Recording: yes

Quick agenda: intro, current topology, constraints (egress/data residency), private endpoints & peering options, regions & latency, next steps.

00:00:03 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, with Diego and Priya from our solutions engineering team. How's everyone doing?
00:00:12 Alexei Romanov: Morning, yeah good — a bit crammed but excited to get into this. We've got a hard timeline for Q1 production gating so we need to understand network posture.
00:00:24 Diego Alvarez: Awesome. Quick check — are you looking at Private deployment or Dedicated reserved capacity?
00:00:31 Priya Desai: We're evaluating both. Our initial requirement is private connectivity inside our VPCs, and likely a dedicated pool if latency/value look right. Security wants zero public egress for inference traffic.
00:00:45 Tom Broussard: To be specific, all model calls must go over our transit gateway and never traverse the public internet. We have a strict egress filter.
00:00:56 Diego Alvarez: Understood. That's a common pattern — we support private endpoints and Transit Gateway peering. Can you describe your current transit architecture?
00:01:06 Elena Park: Sure. We have three AWS accounts — prod, infra, and shared-services. Prod lives in us-west-2 for serving, and we have eu-central-1 for EU customers. We peer via a central transit gateway in the infra account. All egress flows are inspected there; security chops everything.
00:01:22 Maya Chen: Got it. Two quick things we'll need: CIDR ranges for VPCs and the TGW attachment IDs. We'll use those to validate IP planning and avoid overlap.
00:01:31 Alexei Romanov: We'll get those after the call.
00:01:34 00:01:35 Priya Nair: One design question — do you want a private endpoint per region or a single cross-region endpoint behind peering? Latency and cost tradeoffs emerge pretty quickly.
00:01:46 Priya Desai: Prefer per-region. Latency SLA is 60ms p95 for our user-facing inference calls. EU requests must stay in-region for data residency as well.
00:01:56 Diego Alvarez: Per-region endpoints make sense for that SLA. For dedicated pools we can pin model versions in a region; for hosted we can route via private endpoints with regional routing policies.
00:02:07 Marcus Li: From procurement side we need clarity on how billing works for dedicated capacity — is it billed per cluster or per token when private?
00:02:16 Maya Chen: Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract with monthly commit, regardless of private endpoint use; hosted is usage-based. We'll send a detailed pricing table.
00:02:24 Tom Broussard: On encryption — we use customer-managed KMS and HSM for key lifecycle. How does Redwood integrate?
00:02:33 Priya Nair: We support KMS integration for private deployments and can integrate with customer KMS for model-at-rest keys. For hosted we manage keys; for private deployments inside your VPC we can use your KMS/HSM — we will capture the key IDs and grant cross-account access as needed.
00:02:49 Elena Park: Is there an audit trail for all requests and who accessed what? We need to map that to our SIEM.
00:02:56 Diego Alvarez: Yes — we emit audit logs and request traces. For Private deployments we can ship logs to your S3 bucket or push via our secure forwarder into your SIEM; we also have token-level cost and latency breakdowns.
00:03:10 Alexei Romanov: Great. One more compliance detail — do you have SOC 2 + ISO artifacts?
00:03:16 Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include SOC 2 and ISO artifacts in the security pack. We'll also include our network runbook and details on RBAC/SSO integration.
00:03:25 00:03:27 Marcus Li: Are there restrictions on which regions Redwood supports for private endpoints? We have strict EU-availability needs.
00:03:36 Priya Nair: We support private endpoints in major regions including us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1. For some specialized regions we may need an on-prem or Private deployment package.
00:03:54 Priya Desai: If we go dedicated we'd like to host in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Any additional traffic for routing between the two will traverse the TGW?
00:04:03 Diego Alvarez: Yes, traffic between your prod VPCs and our dedicated subnets will go over peering attachments. If you prefer, we can also provision regional dedicated pools to keep traffic local.
00:04:16 Tom Broussard: How do you handle IP ranges? We need predictable IP allocation to set firewall rules.
00:04:23 Priya Nair: We'll provide a suggested IP plan with /27 blocks for endpoints and dedicated worker subnets. We also support NAT-less setups — endpoints are interface ENIs in your VPC so no outbound NAT needed for model traffic.
00:04:36 Elena Park: That helps. Egress rules still need to be strict — what about health checks and telemetry? Any calls that leave region?
00:04:44 Diego Alvarez: Health checks for the private deployment are over the peered link. Telemetry can be forwarded to your collector — nothing needs to traverse the public internet unless you opt into our hosted analytics.
00:04:56 Alexei Romanov: What about automated failover if a region goes down? Do you support warm standby in a different region?
00:05:04 Maya Chen: Yes, our rollout policies allow failover: we can have warm replicas in another region and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if capacity becomes constrained. For dedicated customers we can set failover policies and cross-region replication of model artifacts.
00:05:20 Priya Desai: Okay, pricing for cross-region standby?
00:05:24 Maya Chen: Standby would be additional reserved capacity and storage for model artifacts. We'll put numbers in the pricing sheet, but expect incremental monthly cost.
00:05:34 00:05:36 Marcus Li: Procurement question — contract terms for private deployments, is there a minimum term?
00:05:41 Maya Chen: Dedicated typically has a 6- to 12-month commitment; Private (on-prem/VPC) is an enterprise license with custom term. We'll include options.
00:05:51 Tom Broussard: Networking detail — do the private endpoints require cross-account role assumptions? We run strict IAM boundaries.
00:05:58 Priya Nair: We support two patterns: 1) interface endpoints created in your account that connect to Redwood-managed ENIs in a partner account with strict SG rules; or 2) we deploy a minimal agent in your infra under bring-your-own-image which uses IAM roles for access. Both patterns can be audited and constrained.
00:06:18 Elena Park: The first pattern sounds better for us. No extra agents.
00:06:23 Diego Alvarez: Great. We'll propose the interface endpoint flow — it's the cleanest from an operations perspective.
00:06:28 Alexei Romanov: Any limitations on concurrency per endpoint? We plan bursts during business hours for inference.
00:06:35 Diego Alvarez: We'll size dedicated pools per expected RPS and supply autoscaling buffers. For interface endpoints themselves there's no hard concurrency cap — it's the backend pool capacity that matters. We'll share recommended throughput per endpoint and socket tuning.
00:06:50 Priya Desai: Security — are we allowed to bring our own TLS certs?
00:06:55 Priya Nair: Yes, you can bring certs for TLS termination in some patterns; for interface endpoints it's mutual TLS between your VPC and the Redwood ENIs. We'll detail certificate flows.
00:07:08 Marcus Li: Is there any SNAT required for S3 access for model artifacts? We prefer VPC endpoints to avoid internet egress for S3.
00:07:17 Diego Alvarez: You can use VPC endpoints for S3 and KMS, so artifacts stay in-region. We'll advise on S3 bucket policies for cross-account access.
00:07:27 00:07:30 Alexei Romanov: Let's dig into a failure mode: If your backend needs to fall back to a hosted model because dedicated capacity exhausted, does traffic leave our VPC?
00:07:38 Maya Chen: If you have fallbacks configured, traffic could be routed to a hosted-compatible endpoint. We can avoid public egress by having that hosted fallback behind a private endpoint in another region — but that would still traverse our carrier network and may touch additional jurisdictions. We'll flag it in the design.
00:07:55 Tom Broussard: Jurisdictions are key. Any call routed to us-east-1 from EU would violate data residency. We need explicit routing policies per route.
00:08:03 Priya Nair: We have routing policies by region and tenant; we can pin EU customer traffic to EU-only pools and disable cross-region fallback.
00:08:12 Elena Park: Excellent. Latency targets — you said 60ms p95. Can Redwood commit to this in eu-central-1?
00:08:20 Diego Alvarez: We'll run a short benchmark during the trial. From our experience, dedicated pools in eu-central-1 can meet that SLA for chat/completion calls with model variants optimized for lower latency. We'll include baseline test scripts.
00:08:34 Alexei Romanov: Who runs the benchmark, Redwood or Harrington?
00:08:38 Priya Desai: Prefer joint — we will run traffic from our prod VPC into the test endpoints.
00:08:44 Maya Chen: Joint run sounds good. We'll provide a script and a workload profile.
00:08:49 00:08:52 Marcus Li: Back to procurement — data egress costs, who bears egress between regions?
00:08:59 Maya Chen: Egress costs depend on topology: if traffic flows inside your VPC via peering to our dedicated subnets, egress is essentially internal — you'd pay TGW data charges and any inter-region data transfer. We'll provide an estimate for expected GB/day.
00:09:13 Priya Desai: We'll need a sample monthly bill estimate for budgeting.
00:09:17 Maya Chen: We'll add that.
00:09:19 00:09:22 Elena Park: Do you have any references for similar setups? We're in regulated fintech and would like to see a prior deployment for compliance posture.
00:09:31 Maya Chen: We can share an anonymous case study and network topology for a fintech customer with SOC 2 constraints. We'll include contact details for a technical reference.
00:09:41 Diego Alvarez: A couple of quick technical notes I want to capture — the endpoint ENIs will need security groups allowing only your prod subnets. We'll supply the exact ports and cidr lists. Health checks will be TCP-based on X port.
00:09:55 Priya Desai: Are there any ephemeral IPs we need to allow?
00:09:58 Diego Alvarez: We'll avoid ephemeral IPs by using static ENIs and assigned private IPs. For autoscaling workers we do allocate from our reserved subnets but that traffic stays behind the peering.
00:10:09 Tom Broussard: Okay. On the identity side, we require SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
00:10:16 Priya Nair: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. For Private/VPC accounts we can integrate with your IdP and map roles for RBAC.
00:10:25 Marcus Li: Any third-party vendor dependencies? We have a strong vendor review.
00:10:30 Maya Chen: Nothing critical — we rely on standard cloud networking and your KMS. We'll include a vendor summary for your procurement team.
00:10:37 00:10:40 Alexei Romanov: Time to talk about timelines — our internal target is a pilot by 2029-01-15. Realistic?
00:10:47 Maya Chen: For a short 1-week dedicated trial in two regions, yes. We can standby a pool once we get CIDRs and decide model sizing.
00:10:55 Priya Desai: We'll aim to get CIDRs and TGW attachments by 2028-12-19.
00:11:00 Diego Alvarez: Perfect. We'll also ask for a test account and a list of sample prompts for benchmarks.
00:11:06 00:11:09 Alexei Romanov: One more thing — we use strict egress logs and packet capture for audits. Any support for packet-level logging?
00:11:17 Priya Nair: We don't ship full packet captures, but we provide request-level traces and full audit records. For packet captures you'd run VPC traffic mirroring on your side and feed it to the SIEM.
00:11:29 Tom Broussard: That works.
00:11:32 00:11:35 Marcus Li: Competitors aside, what's Redwood's differentiator for private deployments?
00:11:40 Maya Chen: Production-first tooling: cost breakdowns at token level, rollout policies, and tight observability (per-route latency/cost) plus flexible deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private) with consistent APIs.
00:11:53 Alexa voice or Speaker glitch: [inaudible 00:11:55]
00:12:00 Diego Alvarez: Wrapping up — proposed immediate deliverables: architecture diagram for interface endpoints over your TGW, pricing sheet, security pack, benchmark scripts, and a kickoff for the deep dive.
00:12:12 Elena Park: Sounds good. One ask: include concrete IP allocations so our firewall folks can pre-configure rules.
00:12:18 Maya Chen: Yes — we'll include a sample IP plan.
00:12:22 Priya Desai: Also include the tagging strategy — we use strict tags for billing and ownership.
00:12:28 Maya Chen: We'll recommend tagging standards for endpoints and resources.
00:12:32 00:12:35 Alexei Romanov: Great — excited to move forward.
00:12:38 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the technical deep dive for next week.
00:12:45 Meeting closed.
